title: Tinman harness plan
description: The canonical YAML representation of a recorded or authored flow. A plan is either the full form, carrying a flow of run and tui entries, or the shorthand form, carrying one command and its steps. Both normalize to the same parsed plan. Referenced by features/harness-plan.feature and features/plan-shorthand.feature.

sandbox.description: Backend-neutral sandbox specification. Omitted means the secure defaults: empty home, network denied.

tui.description: Shorthand form: the single terminal program this plan drives.

steps.description: Shorthand form: the steps driving the program named by tui.

sources.description: What this plan was written from, and the terms that came with it. A plan built from a program's own help needs no entry; a plan built from somebody else's documentation carries the source and its licence, because the page is their work and the plan travels further than the session that wrote it. Absent where nothing outside the binary was read, which is the ordinary case.

flowEntry.description: One process in the flow: a plain command, or a terminal program driven by steps.

status.description: The exit status this command is expected to leave. Omitted means 0. A command-line program's failure is often the behaviour under test, so an expected non-zero status passes the step and any other status fails it.

stdin.description: Text fed to the command's standard input, which is closed afterwards. Omitted means standard input is empty and closed immediately.

step.description: One semantic action or assertion against the driven program.

activate.description: Activate the region a locator resolves to. A bare string is the locator's name.

fill.description: Enter a value into the textbox carrying a label.

press.description: Send one key to the program.

expect.description: Assert the screen carries a text, or that a locator resolves to a region. A bare string is the text. The locator form is the same locator `activate` addresses a region with, and a region's name is its content in this model, so naming a role and a name is how an expectation states a value.

conforms.description: Attest the whole terminal object model against a layout scantling at this path. A locator names one region and a text names one string, where a layout constrains which regions exist, where they sit and how they are drawn, so a program drawing the right things in the wrong places fails here and passes every other step.

capture.description: Collect the items of a pane into named structured data.

locator.description: Addresses a region of the terminal object model by role and name. An absent role matches any role.

binding.description: How this locator was arrived at when the plan was recorded. An inferred name that bound on its own reads `exact`; one that needed its parent region to disambiguate reads `scoped`; one the deterministic pass could not confirm reads `ordinal`, and the locator addresses a position within its role rather than a name. A hand-authored locator omits the key. Recording the rung keeps a weak locator legible: a plan whose locators are mostly `ordinal` reports that inference did badly on that screen, and a green run never will.
